subject: Dedicated capacity vs hyperscaler GPUs — follow-up & next steps
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Alexandra Jones <alex.jones@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity vs hyperscaler GPUs — recap and recommended next tests

Alex — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

- Key asks from ACME: predictable per-request latency for real-time chat, stable throughput for nightly batch embedding jobs, and a hard requirement for data isolation + audit logs.
- Your constraint: existing hyperscaler commitments (reserved instances) that you want to evaluate against Dedicated for predictability and unit cost.
- Preliminary Redwood differentiators we discussed: reserved Dedicated pools with SLA-backed capacity, autoscaling/burst options, built-in KV/prefix caching to improve token cost, and traceable audit logs + KMS integrations for compliance.

Proposed next tests (short):
1) Complimentary 2-week Dedicated spike (non-production) to measure tail latency and sustained throughput for your mixed workload.
2) Side-by-side latency/cost benchmark vs your hyperscaler reserved instance baseline using the same model/quantization profile.
3) Validate failover: route to a compatible model variant when Dedicated capacity is constrained and measure failover latency.

I've attached a short comparison deck and a proposed benchmark plan. Laura will follow up with pricing for a 2-week reserved pool and options for a month-long proof-of-concept.

Next steps: could you confirm the model(s) and expected concurrency (peak qps) for chat + nightly job sizes? Also confirm the preferred start date for the test window.

Thanks —
Markus
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-quick-comparison.pdf (pdf), acme-benchmark-plan.pdf (pdf)
From: Alexandra Jones <alex.jones@acme.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity vs hyperscaler GPUs — recap and recommended next tests

Thanks Markus — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Models: we want to test both a 13B chat model (for low-latency front-line chat) and a 70B embedder for nightly batch jobs.
- Expected concurrency: chat peak ~120 concurrent requests (burstable to 200 for promo periods). Nightly batch ~400k embeddings over a 2-3 hour window.
- Constraints: our procurement team needs a clear cost comparison (TCO) and a written capacity guarantee if we move to Dedicated.

We can start the tests the week of Nov 30. Procurement will want pricing and an SLO note for capacity — can Laura share a template SLA + pricing options?

Also: can you include any existing customer references who moved off hyperscaler reserved instances to Redwood Dedicated? A short case study would be helpful for procurement.

Appreciate it —
Alex
VP, AI Platform
ACME Corp
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:17:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: pricing/SLA options for ACME POC

Markus/Laura — noted ACME requirements. Quick ideas to prepare before the kickoff: 

- Offer Tiered Dedicated pool: guaranteed baseline (e.g., 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs) + burstable buffer (soft limit) that we can size to their peak. Provide a documented latency SLO for tail p95/p99 and a credit policy for missed SLOs.
- Pricing: two alternatives — (A) monthly reserved commit with discount vs on-demand; (B) short-term POC pricing (30 days) with a fixed capacity and usage reconciliation. For procurement, include both unit ($/token and $/GPU-hour) and blended TCO scenarios compared to their reserved hyperscaler pricing assumptions.
- Case study: reference AcmeHealth (anonymized) that moved from reserved hyperscaler instances to Dedicated and realized ~18% lower unit cost with better tail-latency stability.

I'll draft an SLA template and a one-page TCO worksheet. Markus — can you confirm the exact GPU equivalence ACME expects (A100-80GB vs A100-40GB) so we can align benchmarking?

-Jonas
From: Alexandra Jones <alex.jones@acme.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 11:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity vs hyperscaler GPUs — recap and recommended next tests

That all looks good — thanks. Confirming: start the POC week of Nov 30. We'll lock in the model configs you listed and expect the POC order form + SLA from Laura tomorrow. A 30-minute call on Monday Nov 30 at 9:00am PT to walk procurement through the pricing would be ideal.

Please include the anonymized case study you mentioned for procurement.

Talk Monday —
Alex
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Alexandra Jones <alex.jones@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity vs hyperscaler GPUs — recap and recommended next tests

Alex — thanks for the quick clarifications. We've updated the attached pricing worksheet and benchmark plan to include: 

- Model mapping: 13B chat mapped to our optimized 13B profile (quantized where applicable) and 70B embedder with recommended batching for nightly runs.
- Suggested baseline: 8 x A100-40GB equivalent for baseline Dedicated pool with a 4-GPU burst buffer. This should comfortably handle 120 concurrent chat QPS with room for bursts to 200; nightly embedding window handled by batching.
- SLA: included p95/p99 latency targets and a credit policy. For the POC we propose a short SLA (read-only metrics, no formal credits) and a guaranteed baseline for capacity during the test window. For production, we can offer SLA credits as part of a reserved commit contract.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-pricing.xlsx (xlsx), acme-benchmark-plan.pdf (pdf), redwood-vs-hyperscaler-quick-comparison.pdf (pdf)

Proposed next steps:
- Laura to send POC order form / pricing options and draft SLA by EOD tomorrow.
- ACME to confirm start date (week of Nov 30) and approve test model configs.
- Jonas to prepare benchmark harness and share test scripts/drive folder.

Let me know if you'd like a 30-minute call early next week to walk procurement through the pricing and SLA language.

Best,
Markus
